title: Bat tests positive for rabies in North Stonington | North Stonington | thewesterlysun.com
text:
NORTH STONINGTON����� On Monday, the town announced a bat found on Anthony Road was captured and tested positive for rabies.
Rabies is a fatal disease transmitted to humans through a bite or scratch from an infected animal. Humans can be exposed to the disease when saliva from infected animals comes into contact with open wounds, and mucous membranes such as the eyes, nose, and mouth.
The virus lives in the saliva and brain tissue of infected animals, and unvaccinated cats and dogs could potentially transmit the virus to humans.
There is no known cure for rabies once symptoms appear, but the disease is almost entirely preventable if treated promptly after exposure. Individuals can avoid exposure by refraining from feeding or approaching wild or stray animals, keeping pets up to date with vaccinations, and limiting pets' unsupervised outdoor time.
Residents with questions can contact Ledge Light Health District at (860) 448-4882 or North Stonington Animal Control at (860) 287-2197.
